title: Irrigation and Equipment Response Verification within Safe Authority

content.overview: Equipment verification means checking whether the system performs as intended within an assigned procedure. It does not turn the technician into an electrician, mechanic or hazardous-energy authorized employee. Irrigation verification therefore combines measured delivery and pressure/filtration evidence with a strict operator-care boundary.

vocabulary.definition: How evenly an irrigation system delivers water among representative locations.
The last action explicitly assigned to the operator before servicing, protected access or hazardous-energy controls require another authorized role.
Energy such as pressure, gravity, spring force, heat or electrical charge that can remain after normal shutdown.

sections.title: Measure installed irrigation performance
sections.body: Representative catch volumes, line position, pressure and filtration condition reveal distribution problems that nominal emitter ratings cannot prove.

sections.title: A normal stop is not energy isolation
sections.body: Normal controls do not by themselves establish that unexpected startup or stored energy is controlled for servicing. Protected access, disassembly, guard removal or pressure release are strong boundary cues.

sections.title: Do not expand authority because the repair looks simple
sections.body: The equipment procedure and employer authorization determine what the technician may inspect, reset, clean or adjust. Familiarity or previous experience does not create current authorization.

workedExamples: A far-end irrigation zone tests low; the technician records catch-volume and pressure evidence but escalates a repair that requires powered disassembly.
A faulted fan may be visually inspected under the operator procedure, but opening an electrical enclosure is routed to the qualified role.
commonMistakes: Trusting nominal emitter flow without field verification.
Loosening a pressurized fitting because the pump is off.
Using prior maintenance experience as proof of current authorization.
content.practicalApplication: Run a representative irrigation/equipment verification exercise, identify the last permitted operator action, document any energy/protected-access cue, preserve safe status and create the maintenance handoff.
content.summary: Technician II verifies performance deeply but does not cross servicing, hazardous-energy or protected-access boundaries without explicit authorization.

primaryVisuals.title: Verify performance without crossing the service boundary
primaryVisuals.alt: Irrigation and equipment verification flow measuring installed output, comparing it with the assigned procedure, checking for protected access, hazardous energy, pressure, disassembly or unassigned servicing, then routing to either an authorized operator action or stop-and-escalate handoff.
primaryVisuals.caption: Technician II may verify installed performance deeply, but protected access, hazardous energy, pressure release, disassembly or unassigned servicing are stop-and-escalate cues unless specifically authorized.
